label: H.R. 3444

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: The Tribal Self-Determination and Co-Management in Forestry Act of 2025 directs Federal land management agencies within the Department of the Interior to establish Tribal Co-Management Plans for certain public lands. It also authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to enter into agreements and contracts with Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations to perform specific Forest Service activities, provides training requirements for Department of the Interior employees, and authorizes appropriations of $50,000,000 for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to participate in co-management planning with Interior land management agencies and enter into agreements or contracts with the Forest Service to perform certain land management activities, receive funding, and integrate indigenous knowledge.
Agency heads must establish Tribal Co-Management Plans, and employees involved must complete training regarding indigenous knowledge, tribal history, and federal trust responsibilities.
affected_groups.group: Department of the Interior and Employees

affected_groups.effect: The Secretary of Agriculture is authorized to enter into agreements with tribes, establish minimum agreement thresholds, issue periodic lists of eligible activities, and submit reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Agriculture and Forest Service

key_provisions: Requires the head of each Department of the Interior land management agency to develop a Tribal Co-Management Plan within one year, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior and the Tribal Advisory Committee.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior to ensure that Department of the Interior employees involved in carrying out these plans receive training on incorporating indigenous knowledge, tribal history, and the federal trust relationship.

Authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to enter into agreements or contracts with Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations for the performance of certain Forest Service activities, requiring at least 5 such agreements during the first 4 years.
Sets out criteria and a evaluation process for the Secretary of Agriculture to consider tribal proposals, alongside a formal notice of denial procedure if a request is rejected.

Authorizes $50,000,000 in appropriations for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to carry out Forest Service agreements, and exempts agreements from the Federal Acquisition Regulation while applying Federal Tort Claims Act coverage to participating tribal employees.
Mandates periodic reviews of agreements every 5 years, as well as provisions for reviews and modifications following natural disasters.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact number of acres or specific geographic locations that will ultimately be covered under the co-management plans or Forest Service agreements.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Tribal Self-Determination and Co-Management in Forestry Act of 2025 directs Federal land management agencies within the Department of the Interior to establish Tribal Co-Management Plans for certain public lands. It also authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to enter into agreements and contracts with Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations to perform specific Forest Service activities, provides training requirements for Department of the Interior employees, and authorizes appropriations of $50,000,000 for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters how certain federal lands under the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service are managed by formally establishing structured co-management planning and authorizing tribes to directly carry out specific forestry and land management functions through federal agreements.

title: Tribal Self-Determination and Co-Management in Forestry Act of 2025
